newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call rate tad softer on excess liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Manila call rate tad softer on excess liquidity.

text.p: * Borrowings from small banks swell turnover
The Philippine overnight rate dipped to 10.875 percent from 10.90625 percent despite heavy turnover bloated by small banks' borrowings, traders said.

"The market is swamped with excess money. Banks were very cautious, opting to stay liquid during the Christmas season," one trader said. Heavy withdrawals are expected between Christmas and New Year's day.

Banks were initially offering overnight money 50 basis points above the Central Bank's benchmark rate of 10.75 percent, but the rate softened after lenders emerged by midsession. Done rates ranged from 10.8125 to 11.25 percent.
Turnover swelled to 33.473 billion pesos from Tuesday's 26.374 billion pesos.
"Many banks have prepared for the Christmas season by tightening up on granting of loans and hiking their special savings rates to keep themselves liquid," another trader said.
Fresh funds of more than $2 billion have contributed to the already liquid market.
The secondary market for government securities was quiet with rates generally unchanged from the previous levels.
Three-month bills were being bid between 11.5 to 11.75 percent and being offered between 11.40 to 11.50 percent.
Six-month bills were bought at 11.775 to 12.0 and sold at 11.65 to 11.725 percent, and one-year bills were bid at 12.10 to 12.30 and offered at 12.05 to 11.20 percent.
